name: Good Morning
pose: Barbell good morning partway through a hip hinge
accessibilityLabel: Grey mannequin hinging forward with a barbell across the upper back, with hamstrings and spinal erectors highlighted.
prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: original square workout exercise illustration.
Input1 is the canonical identity/style REFERENCE ONLY; create the new exercise below.
Keep EXACT SAME adult pale slate-grey mannequin, oval bald head, natural athletic build, realistic proportions, matte material, short charcoal training shorts and charcoal shoes. Match restrained premium 3D rendering, soft upper-left lighting, light cool-grey #F3F5F7 background and subtle contact shadow.
Only specified exposed primary muscle bellies use muted coral #DF685A. Remove reference biceps highlights; do not highlight joints, bones, secondary muscles or through clothing. No glow or veins.
One whole figure and complete specified equipment, near-orthographic low-distortion camera, square 1024x1024, 7–9% margins. Plausible hands, limbs and support contacts. No text, logos, numbers, arrows, panels, duplicates or gym scenery.

Exercise: BARBELL GOOD MORNING lowered hip hinge. Bar supported across upper trapezius BEHIND neck, closed overhand grips slightly outside shoulders, elbows bent down/back. Feet hip-width, soles flat, knees softly bent about15degrees, hips pushed back, torso inclined30degrees above horizontal, long neutral spine and neck gazing down-forward. One continuous bar, equal modest graphite plates/collars; no bar touching throat. REAR-side three-quarter view clearly showing hinge, flat back, bar upper-trap contact, whole feet and rear thighs. Highlight exposed HAMSTRINGS below shorts and two narrow spinal-erector strips either side of spine on lower back; no lats, biceps or calves; covered glutes uncolored.

review.notes: Bar rests across upper traps behind neck with closed grips; hips back, modest knee bend, neutral back and grounded feet. Actual position is a partial hip hinge, not deepest bottom; label reflects it. Hamstrings and narrow erector regions highlighted.
review.independentNotes: Viewed full image: bar supported behind shoulders with two closed grips, hips shifted back and soft knees; moderate forward inclination correctly described as partial hinge.
